input:
This memo recommends that a three-month pilot of condition sensors should be carried out before any decision is taken on installing sensors across the whole plant. The plant operates a total of 180 pumps. Maintenance records covering a period of 12 months show 1375 h of unplanned downtime, and it is notable that bearing failures account for 38% of the downtime hours.

A sensor set for all 180 pumps has been quoted at $439k installed, plus a further $72k per year. In a vendor trial carried out on a comparable unit, the sensors were reported to cut downtime by 22%; however, it should be emphasised that this is a vendor figure and that it was not measured at this plant. A pilot on 23 pumps would cost $43k over three months, and the 23 pumps would be drawn from the plant's own pump population. Spare-part lead times are unchanged by the sensors, so the pilot would test the detection benefit only.

The memo therefore recommends the three-month pilot. The reliability engineering group owns the pilot and will report before the March capital review, and the decision on full installation is held until the pilot results have been reported and can be considered by the review.

In addition, it should be borne in mind that the downtime record itself provides the baseline against which any improvement would be judged, and the pilot would allow that comparison to be made on a consistent basis, under the plant's own operating and maintenance conditions, rather than relying on results obtained elsewhere.
target:
A three-month pilot of condition sensors on 23 pumps is recommended. The decision on full installation is held until the pilot results are reported, and the reliability engineering group owns the pilot and reports before the March capital review.

The plant runs 180 pumps. Maintenance records for 12 months show 1375 h of unplanned downtime, and bearing failures account for 38% of the downtime hours. A sensor set for all 180 pumps is quoted at $439k installed, plus $72k per year. In a vendor trial on a comparable unit, the sensors cut downtime by 22%; the figure is a vendor figure and was not measured at this plant, and it carries the trial's conditions with it.

The pilot is sized to the failure mode that dominates the record. Bearing failure is the largest single share of downtime hours, and it is the mode the sensors detect. A pilot on 23 pumps at $43k over three months buys the plant's own downtime evidence at a small fraction of the full installed cost, on the pumps and under the maintenance regime the full decision concerns. Spare-part lead times are unchanged by the sensors, so any reduction the pilot shows comes from earlier warning, not from faster repair, and the two effects are not confounded in the pilot's figures. The capital review decides on full installation with the pilot's reported downtime in hand. The pilot reports downtime on the same basis as the maintenance record, so its result reads directly against the baseline the full case is built on.
